question: Distinguish between cost accounting and financial accounting.

points.label: Purpose and users
points.description: Financial accounting reports results and financial position mainly to external users; cost accounting ascertains, controls and reduces costs for management.

points.label: Statutory requirement
points.description: Financial accounting is compulsory by law; cost accounting is largely voluntary except where cost records are prescribed.

points.label: Analysis
points.description: Financial accounts show results for the business as a whole; cost accounts analyse costs by product, job, process or department.

points.label: Nature of figures and reporting
points.description: Financial accounting uses historical figures reported periodically; cost accounting also uses estimates and standards and reports more frequently.
